title: On Linux every lender start copies the host's cs-sandbox into the group, though the image already carries a matching one
foundBy: maintainer, while reviewing the fix for SBX-040, 2026-09-15

evidence.verified:
`lenderBinary` now returns `CS_SANDBOX_LENDER_BIN` and nothing else, so with the variable unset there is no binary to stage. With no binary, TestLenderBoxJoinsOneNetworkAndNothingElse pins `--entrypoint cs-sandbox`, which runs the copy the image carries.

The old default was never used by a test. Every lending test drives the CLI in process through `execRoot`, where the executable is the test binary, and each make target that runs them sets the variable. `make test-smoke` passes all 14 TestAgentReplay cells and TestCLILendKeyLive with it set, and `make check` exits 0. A lent create on Linux against a full image, which is the new default path, was not run.

resolution: The lender runs the image's own cs-sandbox unless `CS_SANDBOX_LENDER_BIN` names one, so a released cs-sandbox copies nothing into the group. The test tiers still name a binary, because the slim image they boot has none.
details:
When `create` starts a group's lender container on Linux, `lenderBinary` in internal/cli/lend_create.go picks the running cs-sandbox. `lenderBox.stage` then copies that binary, about 10 MB, into `<group>/.lender/`, and the container runs the copy.

For a released cs-sandbox the copy buys nothing. The binary names an image built from its own revision, and image/Containerfile installs the cs-sandbox that made it. The container therefore already holds a matching lender, which is what macOS runs today.

The copy is needed in two cases only. The slim image the test tiers boot carries no cs-sandbox at all, and a developer changing the lender wants their build without rebuilding the image. Both can name a binary with `CS_SANDBOX_LENDER_BIN`, and the Makefile already does for the tiers. The copy is also the step whose shared temporary name caused the race in SBX-040.
